data.narrative:
Amber Bio is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Basem Al-Shayeb and Jacob Borrajo that has raised $26M to date. The valuation assessment draws from a comparables universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in the same sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Chai Discovery.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($26M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $65M. The peer-median method could not be deployed due to insufficient comparable datapoints at the same or adjacent stage within the Biotech & Health sector—while 8 private peers exist, none met narrow filtering criteria. Public-comp anchoring similarly could not be applied because Amber Bio's revenue is not on file, precluding a price-to-sales multiple calculation despite a 5.6x median P/S across the three public tickers.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $55M to $75M, centered at $65M. This estimate rests on a single methodological leg, introducing material uncertainty. Key risks include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific company and the limited visibility into comparable transaction multiples at early stages in the sector. Additional leverage could be gained through revenue-generating peer comparisons or access to recent seed and Series A transactions in adjacent biotech subsegments.
